steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Running stitch and back stitch are basic construction stitches; chain, satin and French knots are decorative stitches with distinct visual qualities.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Free-motion machine embroidery drops the feed dogs, allowing you to draw with thread — it requires practice to control speed and direction.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Appliqué attaches fabric shapes to a background fabric — it can be fused, pinned or stitched in place before edge-stitching.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Patchwork and piecing join fabric pieces edge-to-edge; accuracy in cutting and seam allowance is essential for flat, even results.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Create a series of experimental studies exploring hand and machine stitching. Annotate your process. | Research an artist or designer who works with hand and machine stitching. Write a critical analysis of their approach and explain how it has informed your own work. | Evaluate the effectiveness of your experiments with hand and machine stitching. Which approaches were most successful and why?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A range of experimental studies showing different approaches to hand and machine stitching, each annotated with media, technique and purpose. Show development from initial experiments to refined outco | A critical analysis naming a specific artist/designer, using specialist vocabulary, explaining their context and approach, and making clear connections to personal work. | A reflective evaluation identifying successful and less successful experiments, explaining WHY using technical and conceptual language, and showing how evaluation led to further refinement.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Address ALL four Assessment Objectives — AO1 (develop), AO2 (refine), AO3 (record), AO4 (present) Show the FULL creative journey — from initial research to final outcome Annotate your work using specialist vocabulary (not just "I like it") Draw from primary sources wherever possible — real objects, not photos Experiment with a RANGE of media and techniques before selecting Make clear connections between artist research and your own developing work
